definition: A service that holds identities, proves who someone or something is, and hands the app a signed token saying so. Apps trust the provider instead of storing passwords themselves, so one account, one policy and one leaver switch cover every app.
example: Entra ID is the identity provider for the admin portal; the portal stores no passwords at all.

definition: The two standards apps use to talk to an identity provider. OpenID Connect signs a user in and returns an ID token for the app that asked. OAuth 2.0 issues access tokens - signed JWTs - that the app sends to an API, which must check the signature, issuer and audience before trusting any claim.
example: The React admin portal gets an ID token for itself and an access token whose audience is the Node API.

definition: An application's definition in Entra ID: its client ID, redirect URIs, credentials, requested permissions and app roles. Client secrets on it expire after at most two years and are the classic cause of 3am outages; prefer certificates, and better still managed identities or workload identity federation.
example: The admin portal's app registration defines the app roles Catalogue.Editor and Orders.Refund.

definition: An application's identity inside one tenant, created from its app registration: the object you assign users and groups to, grant permissions and roles to, and disable. Shown in the portal as an enterprise application. A managed identity is a service principal whose credentials Azure manages for you.
example: The CI pipeline's service principal holds Contributor on rg-shop-dev only.

definition: Requiring something beyond a password to sign in, such as the Authenticator app, a passkey or a hardware key. It blocks the great majority of account takeovers and is now required for the Azure portal. Admins should use phishing-resistant methods such as passkeys and FIDO2 keys rather than texts or push approvals.
example: The finance director's reused password is useless to the attacker once MFA is required.

definition: Entra ID rules of the form: if this user, app, location, device or risk, then require MFA, require a managed device, or block. Needs Entra ID P1 (about $6 per user per month). Test new policies in report-only mode and always exclude the emergency access accounts. Security defaults are the free, one-switch alternative for small tenants.
example: Admins must use a passkey from a managed device to open the Azure portal; everyone else needs MFA.

definition: A cloud-only admin account excluded from Conditional Access, with a long random password or FIDO2 key kept offline, used only when normal admin sign-in is broken - for example by a bad policy. Keep two, and alert on every sign-in.
example: When a new policy locks out every admin, Priya uses the break-glass account from the safe to roll it back.

definition: A person from another organisation invited into your tenant who signs in with their own organisation's account. You control what they can reach; access reviews or an expiry date remove them when the work ends. Contractors should be guests, not accounts you create and forget.
example: The contractor is invited as a guest to the dev subscription with access that expires at the end of the engagement.

definition: Microsoft's customer identity service: a separate external tenant for consumers to sign up and sign in with email one-time codes or Google and Apple accounts, with your branding and self-service password reset. The first 50,000 monthly active users are free. The successor to Azure AD B2C, which no longer takes new customers.
example: Shoppers sign in to the React Native app through the shop's External ID tenant; staff never share it.
